First of all, I convey warmest greetings to you on the occasion of Janmashtami. So, let's begin our conversation. Sidhant, WION: Hi, sir. Sidhant from WION. Sir, any update on the Nepal situation in terms of the Indian casualties and of course the latest update on the Indian relief material, given the fact that the last military plane left yesterday night. Akansha: Good evening, sir. Sir, in Ukraine, during a press briefing, External Affairs Minister Dr. Jaishankar has said that the Ukrainian conflict will not be solved because somebody is buying or not buying oil, but will be solved by dialogue and diplomacy. Given that Kyiv has repeatedly raised India's purchase of Russian oil, how did India convey its position to President Zelenskyy? And was there any forward movement on Dr. Jaishankar's offer that India can help? I have a second question. This is with regards to the case of domestic worker Vanitha from Tamil Nadu who allegedly was tortured in Kuwait. The embassy intervened after her SOS video. What is her current status? And how is MEA addressing such distress cases of Indian workers in the Gulf? Shailendra, Network 18: Sir, Shailendra Network 18 se. Ek sir, report ye bhi thi ki Nepal ke saath-saath China ne bhi bola hai ki kuch Indian nationals wahan par missing hain. Kya unke baare mein koi update mil payega? [Approximate Translation: Question in Hindi] Sir, Shailendra from Network 18. There was also a report that, along with Nepal, China has said that some Indian nationals are missing there. Will there be any update regarding them? Keshav Padmanabhan, The Print: Thank you, spokesperson. Keshav Padmanabhan here from The Print. Just following up on Akansha's question on Ukraine. We saw that External Affairs Minister Jaishankar was in Moscow for the IRIGC-TEC. Prime Minister Modi met with President Putin. And now, EAM is in Ukraine. So, is there any sort of message that's being conveyed between both parties? Is India sort of trying to be a person conveying messages between both sides? My second question is on Nepal. The Nepalese Foreign Minister has said that, you know, certain countries need to give compensation for global warming, mentioning, you know, India, China, and the US. So, has Nepal actually raised this issue with India so far, sir? Thank you. Sahil Pandey, ANI: Good evening, sir. I'm Sahil Pandey from ANI news agency. Can we have a readout on EAM Jaishankar's meeting with Poland Foreign Minister Sikorski? And also, Balen Shah has thanked India in parliament regarding the aid which we have sent. If you can give us a response. Thank you. Shri Randhir Jaiswal, Official Spokesperson: Okay. So, let's take these questions first. Sidhant, coming to your question about the support that India has so far given to Nepal. You would have seen the press releases and statements and the updates that we have been releasing from time to time, giving you the details. We will continue to provide assistance as per the requirement from the Government of Nepal. We do in the coming days plan to send more forensic kits, Bailey bridges, and other material that are requested by the Government of Nepal. And these details will be shared with you as and when these supplies are undertaken. Yesterday, we had two Indian aircraft flying to Kathmandu along with 21 tons of relief material. You would have seen those visuals as also our statement. Till now, we have supplied around 95 tons of relief material on seven aircrafts. So that is, that is all, that is what we have given so far. In addition to the relief material, we've also sent 54 personnel to support relief and rescue efforts in Nepal. This comprises 30 tunnel experts, 19 forensic experts, and a five-member medical team. Our rescue and forensic teams are deployed on the ground, and they are closely working with the Nepalese authorities. As per our current information, 275 Indian nationals remain missing. We continue to be in close touch with the Nepali Government and with the Ministry of Home Affairs here and the relevant or concerned state governments in India as well. We have been releasing regularly the names of Indians who have been rescued. You would have seen some of those updates. And we deeply appreciate the efforts of the Nepal authorities in this regard. So far 166 Indian nationals have been rescued in Nepal. I also wish to add here that so far 1,907 Indian nationals have safely crossed into Nepal from China. And as per official sources in China, there are no Indian travelers who are stranded in the Tibet Autonomous Region in China. So, any Indian national who was there has left China or ... Tibet Autonomous Region. So that is the update on Nepal, and we shall keep you updated with more details as and when those are available. Akansha, you have two questions. First on oil. On energy imports or sourcing, you are well aware, you know, what guides it. Our national interest guides our energy purchases and the imperative for us to meet the energy requirements of 1.4 billion people. That is what guides us, and that will continue to be our policy. The other question you had was... Akansha: The mediation ... Shri Randhir Jaiswal, Official Spokesperson: Okay. So on that, you know, when External Affairs Minister was in Ukraine, he had a press conference. In the press conference, he gave a detailed readout of his discussion and India, Government of India's thought on various issues on the bilateral side and also in the context of the developments that are happening in the Ukraine-Russia conflict. Let me say that External Affairs Minister, he visited Ukraine, Kyiv on 3rd September. He met with Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha, as also he called on President Zelensky. During his conversations, External Affairs Minister noted that India has consistently maintained that this is not an era of war and solution will not emerge from the battlefield. He also underlined Prime Minister Modi's comments that endless war must now give way to the end of war, noting that it is for the parties involved to find a way. He further added that if India can be of any help in any manner to bring the war to an end, it was ready to do so. In consonance with Prime Minister's recent call for an end to the war, EAM's visit was focused on exploring the prospects of dialogue and diplomacy. On your other question about the domestic worker, our Embassy as and when they came to know of this particular issue, they gave her a helping hand and as of now, you would have seen some of those videos, she is with our Embassy now and we remain committed to doing our best for the wellbeing, safety and welfare of Indian nationals abroad. Shailendra, to your question. Dekhiye humare paas jo abhi jo ank hai, 275 Bharatiya nagrik lapata hain. Usmein ho sakta hai.. Chunki kuch chunki ek dynamic sa situation hai, thoda bahut upar neeche kahein koi nayi khabar aati rehti hai. Ismein 275 mein 49 woh log hain jo jo Cheen mein bhi unke list pe missing hain jo humari Embassy hai wahan par. Toh kul milakar 275 hai, usmein lekin 49 log hain jo jo Cheen ki taraf unko wahan par jo missing hai woh bhi isi mein hai, 49. [Approximate Translation: Answer in Hindi] Shailendra, to your question. Look, the figure we have at the moment is that 275 Indian nationals are missing. Since this is a dynamic situation, the number may fluctuate slightly as new information keeps coming in. Of these 275, there are 49 people who are also on the list of those reported missing in China, according to our Embassy there. So, the total is 275, but within that figure, there are 49 people who are also among those reported missing by the Chinese side. 49. Keshav, on Ukraine, you would have seen the press statement in the press conference by External Affairs Minister where he outlined our point of view as also in response to Akanksha's question I just told you, you know, that India stands ready to do whatever it can ... is extending its help to end the war in Ukraine. On your question regarding the comments made by the Foreign Minister of Nepal, let me say that you know, in the wake of this tragedy, we have extended our solidarity and support to the Government and people of Nepal as a close friend and partner. India responded promptly as you have seen and we will continue to support rescue, relief, reconstruction and recovery efforts in the country. In particular, the remarks that you referred to, I understand that a clarification also has been issued by the Nepalese side. Having said that, let me say that India has consistently maintained that climate change is a common challenge and action in this regard must be based on the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities and respective capabilities. Developed countries who historically are responsible for the emissions and have contributed overwhelmingly to this present crisis must take lead in reducing emissions and supporting developing countries by way of finance and technology transfer to meet this challenge. Sahil, your question regarding meeting with the Polish Foreign Minister, External Affairs Minister is in Warsaw and he has meetings there, several meetings. We will keep you updated with these details. On the Prime Minister of Nepal, we have seen that the Prime Minister of Nepal has thanked us for our support. As you would have seen, our Prime Minister when this tragedy struck, he spoke to Prime Minister of Nepal and conveyed that India stands shoulder-to-shoulder and extends all its support to Nepal in this time of crisis, and it will offer whatever help is required and we are happy that we are able to give a helping hand to our friends and partners and to our people of Nepal. Yeshi Seli, Business India: This is Yeshi Seli from Business India. The Lord Mayor of Birmingham, Zaker Choudhry, who hails from Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, during the Independence Day celebrations of Pakistan in Birmingham had said that Kashmir belongs to them and that India and Pakistan should talk about it and sit on the table and talk about it. What is MEA's response on that? And how many Heads of State are we expecting in the upcoming BRICS Summit? Kallol Bhattacherjee, The Hindu: Kallol Bhattacherjee from The Hindu, sir. We are just a few days away from the BRICS Summit, so in that context I want to know, has there been a communication from Bangladesh whether Prime Minister Tarique Rahman would be participating, and if not him, then who is going to represent Bangladesh in the BRICS Summit? In that similar context, I would also like to mention that there are several interviews of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina that are appearing in the Indian media. So, the timing is pretty interesting of these interviews, so if you have any comments on that please. Siddhant, CNN-News18: Hi sir, I'm Siddhant from CNN-News18. Sir, one India-funded project in Maldives is in news these days, if you can share some details about that. Thank you. Akhilesh Suman, DD News: Sir, I am Akhilesh Suman from DD News. Prime Minister Narendra Modi met Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of SCO Summit, you were also there. So, when Prime Minister said that this to end the war, not to continue the war, that means that was there any signal from Putin's side that what is his bottom line and how he wants to end the war? Neeraj, News18 India: Sir, Neeraj, News18 India se. Sheikh Hasina ne News18 India se bhi baat cheet ki hai aur unhone ek kaha hai ki koi bhi back channel understanding Rahman sarkar ke saath nahi hai jo unhone December mein lautne ki ghoshna ki hai. Aur unki ek maang hai ki personal security wahan mile, access to lawyers mile, independent judiciary aur fair trial ho. Toh kya unhone is baare mein Bharat Sarkar ko itla kiya hai, koi jankari aap logon ko di hai? Aur ek doosra sawal yeh hai ki Mahan Air ki seedhi udaanein band ho gayi hain yudh ke baad aur Amriki sanction ke baad. Humein jo jankari mili hai Iran ke sutron se woh unhone Videsh Mantralay ko bheja hai prastav ki seedhi udaan shuru ki jaye. Aisa koi prastav aaya hai? [Approximate Translation: Question in Hindi] Sir, Neeraj from News18 India. Sheikh Hasina has also spoken to News18 India, and she has said that there is no back-channel understanding with the Rahman government regarding her announcement to return in December. One of her demands is that she be provided personal security there, access to lawyers, an independent judiciary, and a fair trial. So, has she informed the Government of India about this? Have you received any information from her regarding this? And secondly, direct Mahan Air flights have stopped after the war and following the American sanctions. We have received information from Iranian sources that they have sent a proposal to the Ministry of External Affairs to resume direct flights. Has any such proposal been received? Shri Randhir Jaiswal, Official Spokesperson: So first, Yeshi, regarding your comments by the... Lord Mayor of Birmingham. Now on Kashmir, you know where India stands. The whole of Jammu, Kashmir and Ladakh are parts of India, which are integral to India and inalienable parts of India. That is what I have to say. As far as our policy towards Pakistan is concerned, you know very well where we are on this particular matter. On the number of leaders etc. visiting, we are still few days away, but we will keep you updated on the visitors who are coming for the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi. Kallol, on the participation from Bangladesh side, I have no update to share with you. The other question that you had was about the interviews etc. that are appearing. I have no comments to make on that. Siddhant, you are referring to a project which is, in a way, a historic project. You know that India is a leading development partner for Maldives. We have undertaken several projects in the country, which continue to bring lot of value to the people of Maldives. The Greater Male Connectivity Project is a project which connects the capital Male with three islands. This has seen significant progress, and the first segment of the Greater Male Connectivity Project has been completed. The 2 km bridge over deep waters from Male to another island, which is Villimalé, has been completed and on 30th August. The President of Maldives along with other dignitaries, they took a walk on this particular bridge which connects the two islands. In a sense, it was a historic day for Maldives because for the first time in their history that anybody is walking between the two islands on foot. So that was, you know, very significant from the perspective of the people of Maldives. Let me also tell you that this particular project, it was envisaged in 2021. It's a 6.7 km project which has both bridge and road component to it and is being developed by Afcons. It is expected to be completed by 2026, and once it we are able to complete the project, it has the potential to unleash the economic potential of the area. The total cost of the project stands at around US dollars 500, and it's a stellar example of the Indian assistance that is being rendered to Maldives under our neighborhood first policy. Akhilesh, your question... see, India has always maintained that we are on the side of peace. This is not an era of war. Prime Minister when he met President Putin in Bishkek, he underlined and he said that endless war should now give way to end of war. So he reiterated our position, India's position that no solution lies on the battlefield and India wants that there should be peace in the region as elsewhere so that there is common progress an

Log in here » PRAGUE (AP) — A political group led by Prime Minister Andrej Babiš was leading Saturday in the Czech Republic’s first round of voting to fill one-third of the seats in Parliament’s upper house, the Senate. With votes from more than 93% of polling stations counted, the centrist ANO (YES) movement led of the populist billionaire could have the most candidates, 13, advancing to next week’s runoffs. ANO hopes to make gains in the 81-seat Senate, which is controlled by pro-Western opposition parties. Twenty-seven Senate seats are up for grabs. Czech Republic's Prime Minister Andrej Babis talks to media after casting his vote during senate and local elections in Pruhonice, Czech Republic, Friday, Oct. 9, 2026. (AP Photo/Petr David Josek) Up to six candidates could reach the 50% threshold to win seats outright, none of them from ANO, according to the preliminary results released by the Czech Statistics Office. That could leave 21 seats to be decided in the runoffs between the top two finishers in each race. Parliament’s lower house dominates the legislative process, but the Senate plays an important role in passing constitutional amendments and approving Constitutional Court judges. In separate local elections, various independent candidates and groupings appeared to be winning most seats nationwide, a traditional result. ANO was heading for victory in some regional capitals, but not in Prague. The elections are the first test for Babiš since he returned to power after a decisive victory in parliamentary elections in October 2025. Babiš has formed a governing coalition with two small political groups whose agenda includes reducing support for Ukraine and rejecting some key European Union policies.
